clue.text: Leave West-Country banker without a record

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the river's letters go around the record

parts.note: a river has banks, so a banker is a river; the Dart flows through Devon in England's West Country
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Someone quits a job at a bank in the south-west of England, leaving no record behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' suggests money but means a river. 'Without' is used in its old sense of outside, so the river goes round the record.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave a place is to go away from it, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Retreat is clearly no advantage

explanation.surface: Pulling back from a position is plainly not a winning move.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw back is to retreat (a phrasal verb); a drawback is a disadvantage, the opposite of an advantage.

clue.text: Sorry! What did you say?

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a polite apology and a request for someone to repeat themselves.

clue.text: Charge and overcharge

explanation.definitionFit: To rush is to charge forward in attack; to rush a customer is slang for overcharging them.

clue.text: Unimportant if the verb is intransitive

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson declares something irrelevant because the verb takes no object.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means cost or distance does not matter; literally, an intransitive verb takes no grammatical object.

clue.text: Confidentially, it's not on the disc

explanation.surface: A remark made privately is something not captured on a recording.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarks made privately are not for publication; literally, something absent from a gramophone disc is not recorded.

clue.text: Complaint offensive to a vegetarian

explanation.surface: A grumble that a meat-free diner would find objectionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a grievance or grumble; also meat from cattle, which a vegetarian refuses.

clue.text: Trees planted by mormon officials

explanation.surface: Church leaders of the Latter-day Saints plant trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Elder bushes bear elderberries; senior lay officers in the Mormon church hold that title.

clue.text: Mongolian sailors

parts.note: a tar is slang for a sailor; two of them make the plural
a second tar, another sailor, completing the pair

explanation.surface: Seamen from the steppes of central Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartars were Turkic and Mongol peoples of central Asia, so the word serves for a Mongolian.

clue.text: Stop legal detention

explanation.surface: Police halt someone and take them into lawful custody.
explanation.definitionFit: To halt or check something is to arrest it; also the act of taking a suspect into custody.

clue.text: Lawbreaker sees purpose in proposal

indicators.note: in places the aim inside the proposal, one word cut open to hold the other

parts.note: an offer is a proposal
an end is a purpose or aim

explanation.surface: A criminal sees a motive behind a suggestion made to them.
explanation.definitionFit: A criminal who breaks the law is an offender, a synonym.

clue.text: Aim to condemn? Quite otherwise!

indicators.note: otherwise means in a different way, so the letters of the first three words are arranged in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone intends to denounce, but the result is the very reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite otherwise' rearranges AIM TO CONDEMN and also says the result is the opposite of condemning: praise.
explanation.definitionFit: Praise is the opposite of condemnation, which the clue's 'quite otherwise' describes.

clue.text: Either way, it's a mistake

indicators.note: reading forwards or backwards gives the same word, which is what either way announces

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Whichever way you look at it, an error was made.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a silly blunder or gaffe.

clue.text: Maureen is offered tea or coffee

parts.note: Mo is a short form of the name Maureen
cha (or char) is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: A woman called Maureen is asked whether she wants tea or coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a type of coffee, originally from the Yemeni port of that name.

clue.text: In the bazaar I acquired items for a song

indicators.note: In tells the solver the word sits inside the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: At a market someone bought goods very cheaply, for a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For a song' suggests cheapness, but 'song' is the definition; 'items for a' is link padding.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song in an opera.

clue.text: Alluring lady appears sixty minutes after midnight

parts.note: sixty minutes is an hour
an hour after midnight is one o'clock, and I is Roman one

explanation.surface: A seductive woman turns up at one in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: In Islamic tradition a houri is a beautiful maiden of paradise, so by extension any alluring woman.

clue.text: Dunderhead upset wise French artist

parts.note: the head of 'dunder' is its first letter, D

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the word for wise upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: sage means wise

explanation.surface: A fool upsets a clever French painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dunderhead' looks like an insult, but it splits as the head of 'dunder'; 'upset' turns the word for wise backwards, giving EGAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Degas was a French Impressionist painter.

clue.text: EEC standard currency in Germany and in France

parts.note: common means standard or ordinary
the mark was Germany's currency before the euro
et is French for and

explanation.surface: A remark about Europe's trading bloc and its standard money in Germany and France.
explanation.definitionFit: The European Economic Community was popularly called by that name in Britain.

clue.text: Communist disinformation offers a fool support

parts.note: git is British slang for a fool
a prop is a support

explanation.surface: Red propaganda gives an idiot something to lean on.
explanation.definitionFit: Political propaganda, especially of the Soviet kind, from Russian agitatsiya and propaganda.

clue.text: Jack was sick after being attacked

indicators.note: after puts the piece for being ill behind the donkey

parts.note: a jack is a male donkey, an ass
ailed means was sick

explanation.surface: A sailor fell ill after being set upon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' suggests a sailor (Jack Tar) but means a male donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail is to attack, so the past tense matches.

clue.text: Sue has to fetch youngsters in care

parts.note: to bring is to fetch
children in someone's care are their charges

explanation.surface: A woman named Sue must collect the children she looks after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sue' reads as a woman's name but is the verb to take legal action.
explanation.definitionFit: To sue is to take someone to court, to start legal proceedings against them.

clue.text: Speaker makes court umpire rise

parts.note: to court is to woo

indicators.note: in a down clue rise means the word reads from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: ref, short for referee, is an umpire

explanation.surface: A tennis umpire is made to stand up by someone speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests tennis but is the verb to woo.
explanation.definitionFit: A woofer is a loudspeaker for low frequencies.

clue.text: Loathing headgear of scarlet hue

parts.note: a hat is headgear
scarlet is a shade of red

explanation.surface: Disgust at a bright red hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Loathing is intense dislike, a synonym.

clue.text: Appeal to prohibit port in Scotland

parts.note: O is an exclamation of appeal, as in 'O Lord'
to ban is to prohibit

explanation.surface: A plea to close a Scottish harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Oban is a ferry port on the west coast of Scotland.

clue.text: Road and rail transport

parts.note: a car is a road vehicle
RY is an abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Goods are moved by road and by train.
explanation.definitionFit: To transport something is to carry it, a synonym.

clue.text: Way old architect initially constructed a colonnade

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: An old-time architect started by building a covered walkway.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoa is a covered walk lined with columns in ancient Greek architecture.

clue.text: Some cad made a lady pine

indicators.note: some means only part of the words that follow is used

explanation.surface: A scoundrel made a woman yearn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' looks like a verb meaning yearn but is the timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Deal is sawn softwood timber, especially pine or fir.

clue.text: A little upset when given the facts

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the word for a small amount upside down, reading backwards

parts.note: a tad is a little bit

explanation.surface: Someone is slightly distressed on being told the truth.
explanation.definitionFit: Data are facts and figures collected for reference.

clue.text: Mould a bird in metal? No way!

parts.note: to forge metal is to shape or mould it
a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: An instruction to cast a bird figure in metal is refused outright.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In metal' is no letters; it confirms that forging is shaping metal.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a dismissive refusal, telling someone not to bother.

clue.text: Hardy partner is evergreen

explanation.surface: A tough companion who never fades.
explanation.walkthrough: Stan Laurel was the comic partner of Oliver Hardy.
explanation.definitionFit: Stan was Hardy's comedy partner; the bay tree is an evergreen shrub.

clue.text: Heather chases Lorna's John. That's puzzling

indicators.note: chases means comes after, so the plant follows the hero

parts.note: John Ridd is the hero who loves Lorna in R. D. Blackmore's novel Lorna Doone
ling is a name for heather

explanation.surface: A woman named Heather pursues Lorna's man, which is baffling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' reads as a woman's name but is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Something perplexing or enigmatic, like a riddle.

clue.text: Excelled as an international player

explanation.definitionFit: To cap is to outdo or top; a player capped has been chosen for a national team.
